answer: Treat each cipher as one sybil head. It must anchor in karst, the registry where host keys, enclave measurements and sponsor paths force twins to collide. Every cipher burns lagoon scaled to the square of live heads on its attested host and operator key; clones cannot split one enclave or rent bulk trust, so 1,000 heads mean distinct hardware plus rising lagoon. It breaks if karst merges aliases, enclaves are forgeable, or lagoon is lent.
